issues.title: 0.21.0 hive-mask: second pass swallows prose after an already masked vendor credential
Wrapped base64 still loses harmless binary and misaligns after a preceding alphabet word (0.21.0)
Credentials-only mode masks JavaScript new keyword in a constructor assignment

issues.body:
Credentials-only library 0.21.0 still changes noncredential documentation when the value is followed by a Markdown code-span delimiter. Reproducer:

```js
import { createSyncSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/credentials';
const s = createSyncSanitizer({ credentialsOnly: true, transformation: { mode: 'hive-mask' } });
for (const input of [
  'set `password=<secret>` in the config',
  '`-c model_auto_compact_token_limit=<tokens>` overrides.',
  '`HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_AUTH_AUTHORITY=conventional` to opt out.',
  '`HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0` disables it.',
  '`HIVE_MIND_DISABLE_GIT_AUTH_TRANSPORT=1` opts out.',
]) console.log(s.sanitize(input).text);
```

Expected: all five strings unchanged. Actual: the placeholders or ordinary configuration value are masked, together with the closing backtick (and following space in the `<tokens>` case). Findings are all `context`. The values without backticks already survive apart from the string configuration enum.

These are existing release-note regressions in https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs . Actual credentials in the same prose, including an HTML/script literal after a token key and keyword-prefixed credential values, must remain masked. Downstream PR https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/3741 will retain narrowly scoped exemptions for complete placeholder syntax or exact noncredential configuration name/value pairs while awaiting native handling. Exact known secrets cannot be exempted.
issues.title: Markdown backticks defeat placeholder/configuration exemptions in credentials-only mode
Overlapping Gitleaks finding still masks SharedAccessSignature Authorization scheme (0.21.0)

comments.body:
The short-mask exemption also exposes a related decoded-view gap: `encodedDetect` runs native/context rules on an escaped JSON view without applying the supplied exemption hook there. The view is already clean under the configured policy, but a stale `encoded` finding makes `renderReplacement` substitute `[REDACTED]` for the whole view when recursive sanitization returns it unchanged.

Downstream workaround: for a bounded escaped-JSON finding only, JSON-decode the view and call the configured engine's `inspect()` on it. Exempt the outer finding only if that independent policy inspection reports no findings. Limit recursive exemption inspection to three levels; decoding errors and oversized views retain normal fail-closed handling. Exact known secrets remain unexemptable. The existing escaped-GHCR-log regression must preserve both the record structure and encoded mask.
